facts.text: The test traceability chain links a hazard to a safety requirement, a functional performance requirement, a logical scenario, a test case, a run, a result, and an evidence item in the safety case, in that order.
facts.quote: Hazard, then safety requirement, then functional performance requirement

facts.text: An EMESRT PR-5A objective or an ISO 21815 risk level can serve as the functional performance requirement in the test traceability chain.
facts.quote: functional performance requirement (for example an EMESRT PR-5A objective or an ISO 21815 risk level)

facts.text: ISO 34505 defines test-case attributes comprising unified identifiers, objectives, inputs, steps, platforms, and expected results.
facts.quote: ISO 34505 defines the test-case attributes (unified identifiers, objectives, inputs, steps, platforms, expected results) [12].

facts.text: The minimum manifest stored with each test run includes requirement ID, hazard ID, scenario-family ID and version, concrete parameter vector, operating-domain tags, machine configuration, sensor hardware, extrinsics and calibration, software build or commit, calibration or parameter-set hash, simulator, test-rig or model version, random seed, environmental measurements, execution timestamp, raw-data IDs and checksums, oracle or metric version, verdict, deviations and issues.
